aesthetic.direction: Neo-grotesque product utility: near-black neutral panel + a single electric mint/teal accent, softened by warm cream->amber content thumbnails; wrapped in an indie-utility OpenGraph card (cool blue->warm sand gradient, big two-tone grotesque headline). Sits in the Shottr/Xnapper/CleanShot promo register. NOTE: characterises the marketing composite + its depicted mock UI only — no shipped native surface was observed
aesthetic.cluster_hint: dark-neutral mint-accent menu-bar utility (HOLD — UI evidence is a mock, not a capture)

psychology: Von Restorff effect — one green-highlighted row and one mint-filled slot make the single different thing the focal thing; used well in both the list and the slot strip
Aesthetic-usability effect / 50ms first impression — the OG card is a thesis statement: headline + popover depiction answer 'what is this' (long screenshots, from the menu bar) instantly
Recognition over recall (Jakob's Law) — thumbnail + title + subtitle rows preview the capture target rather than naming it abstractly; a trained list schema
Hick's Law — three clear capture targets rather than an overwhelming source list keeps the decision point small (though this is a curated marketing subset, not necessarily the real app's density)
notes: CRITICAL FOR SYNTHESIS: this source has NO real screenshots — only a 1200x630 OpenGraph marketing card (cover.png) and a 512px app icon (icon.png). The 'app window' on the cover's right is a STYLISED marketing illustration, not a captured surface, evidenced by (a) the popover header mini-icon (plain dark-teal square) not matching the actual app icon (blue scan-frame + download-arrow), and (b) mint/teal UI accent vs system-blue icon glyph. Therefore: (1) lineage is UNKNOWN and unclassifiable — do NOT promote any macOS UI canon or seed a native style cluster from this; open-screen-shot's real framework (likely AppKit/SwiftUI for a menu-bar extra) is NOT evidenced here. (2) era 'big-sur' tags the flat-opaque idiom + the cover's own 'macOS 14+/Sonoma' claim, pre-Liquid-Glass, but is (insufficient-evidence) since it is an illustration. (3) rubric 11/14 and native 5/10 are SOFT scores against a mock and should carry near-zero weight in cross-app aggregation; read the failures[] and defects[]. (4) All measurements are 1x web-composite illustration units, (estimated). To actually digest this app, real captures are needed: the live menu-bar dropdown, the window-picker, the auto-scroll/crop HUD, and Settings. Peer for a proper future comparison: CleanShot X, Shottr, Xnapper (screenshot menu-bar utilities).
